title: A Cascade of Volterra-Operator BBP Transitions in a Correlated Wigner Matrix
abstract: We study a Wigner-type random matrix in which the off-diagonal correlation between entries is generated by a random factor shared among all entries in a given row and column, with the coupling strength held fixed as the matrix size grows. Although the bulk spectral moments remain those of the pure semicircle law, we show that the underlying correlation matrix decomposes into a vanishing bulk together with a countable family of outlier eigenvalues that, at fixed rank $k$, converge to the singular values of a compact Volterra (cumulative-sum) integral operator -- obtained in closed form via the classical Karhunen--Loève expansion of Brownian motion and confirmed numerically to better than one percent across the top twenty such values. Each singular value drives an independent Baik--Ben Arous--Péché (BBP) transition as the coupling strength increases, producing an evenly spaced, discrete hierarchy of critical points -- rather than a single transition -- at each of which one further eigenvalue detaches from the semicircle edge, in close agreement with direct diagonalization. We show that this mechanism generalizes to a broader family of correlation structures, with the critical hierarchy in every case set by the spectrum of an associated compact integral operator.
summary: This paper analyzes a correlated Wigner random matrix whose structure forces its eigenvalues to exhibit a cascade of Baik–Ben Arous–Péché transitions. The key finding is that this entire hierarchy of critical points is precisely determined by the singular values of an underlying compact Volterra integral operator. This establishes a general principle linking structured correlations in random matrices to spectral properties of continuous operators.
main_problem: The study investigates how specific, structured correlations in a Wigner-type random matrix lead to a cascade of eigenvalue transitions rather than the typical single transition.
main_result: The detachment of eigenvalues from the bulk spectrum is governed by the singular values of an associated compact Volterra integral operator, creating a discrete hierarchy of critical points.
method: The analysis uses large-N limits and spectral theory, relating the matrix problem to solving the Karhunen--Loève expansion for Brownian motion to determine the limiting operators.
model_or_system: The model is a Wigner-type random matrix $S$ with off-diagonal correlations generated by shared row/column factors. The analysis extends this to general rank-$r$ deformations involving singular values derived from compact integral operators.
key_observables: Outlier eigenvalues, the critical coupling strengths ($b^{(k)}_c$), and the spectral moments (e.g., $	ext{Tr}(H^2)/N$).
important_parameters: The correlation strength ($\sigma$) and the matrix size ($N 	o \infty$ limit). The transition hierarchy is indexed by $k=1, 2, 3, \dots$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on identifying the large-N limit of the discrete matrix structure with continuous integral operators (Volterra operator) and assumes convergence based on spectral theory conjectures.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the full and bulk eigenvalue spectra showing outliers scaling as $O(N)$, and compare numerically calculated eigenvalues against theoretical predictions derived from singular values for various kernels.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the correlation structure, then deriving the connection to the Volterra operator spectrum via the Karhunen--Loève expansion. It generalizes this finding to show that the entire hierarchy of transitions is dictated by the spectrum of the associated compact integral operator, confirmed across multiple kernel types.
why_interesting: While mathematically rooted in random matrix theory, the concept of spectral rigidity and structured perturbations governing phase transitions has analogues in quantum many-body systems where correlations (like those induced by external fields or interactions) can induce discrete spectral features rather than smooth crossovers.
